subject: tech
title: Save, Find, Delete
about: Where work goes on a computer: saving, files and folders, naming a drawing so you can find it, searching, copying, opening and changing a file, deleting to the trash and asking before the trash is emptied, undo, the cloud as a far-away copy, and the word data. NC K2-DA-01 (store, copy, search, retrieve, modify and delete information) and K2-DA-02 (information stored on a device is data). Read it together: every question and choice is read aloud.
tip: Next time he draws on the tablet, let him pick a name for the file and find it again tomorrow by searching for that name.

cards.q: You drew a picture on the tablet and want to see it tomorrow. What do you do?
cards.note: Saving keeps your work so it is there later. Nothing saved means nothing to find tomorrow.

cards.q: You close a drawing app without saving. What might happen to your drawing?
cards.note: Save before you close. Some apps save for you, but checking is a good habit.

cards.q: What do we call a saved picture or story on a computer?
cards.note: Each saved thing is one file. Pictures, stories and songs are all files.

cards.q: You have ten drawings of dinosaurs. What can hold them all together?
cards.note: A folder is like a paper folder at school. It keeps files that go together in one place.

cards.q: A folder is named Dinosaurs. What goes inside it?
cards.note: The folder name tells you what is inside. Good names make things easy to find.

cards.q: You draw a red truck. What is a good name to save it with?
cards.note: Name a file for what it is. Later you can find red truck fast.

cards.q: You cannot find your drawing called red truck. What can you type in the search box?
cards.note: Searching looks through every file for the name you typed. That is why good names matter.

cards.q: You tap a saved story and it shows up on the screen. What did you just do?
cards.note: Opening a file brings your saved work back so you can see it or change it.

cards.q: You open your story, add a new page, and save again. What did you do to the file?
cards.note: You can open a saved file, change it, and save it again. The new version is kept.

cards.q: You copy your drawing. How many drawings do you have now?
cards.note: Copy makes a second one that looks just the same. The first one stays where it was.

cards.q: You copy a photo into a new folder. What happens to the first photo?
cards.note: Copying never takes the first one away. Now there is one in each place.

cards.q: You delete a drawing you do not want. Where does it go first?
cards.note: Deleting moves a file to the trash. It is not gone for good yet.

cards.q: Oops, you deleted the wrong drawing. Where can you look for it?
cards.note: Open the trash and put the file back. A grown-up can show you how.

cards.q: Emptying the trash makes files go away for good. What do you do before you empty it?
cards.note: Once the trash is emptied, the files cannot come back. Check with a grown-up first.

cards.q: You made a slip and scribbled on your drawing. Which button fixes the last thing you did?
cards.note: Undo takes back your last step. Many apps show it as a curved arrow.

cards.q: Some tablets keep a copy of your photos in the cloud. What is the cloud?
wrong: a rain cloud in the sky
cards.note: The cloud is another computer far away that keeps a copy. If the tablet breaks, the copy is still safe.

cards.q: What is the word for all the information a computer keeps?
cards.note: Data is any information a computer keeps. Photos, stories, game scores: every file is data.
